objective: Fix the consumer side of the timeout seam: implement job_timeout in pipeline/consumer.py so it resolves the frozen wire key timeout_ms first, then the deprecated draft 'timeout' key as fallback, then DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000); add unit tests in tests/test_consumer.py covering timeout_ms primary and both-keys priority while leaving every existing test case in the repo unmodified and green.

concepts: job wire dict shape {id, payload, timeout_ms} passed by reference between producer, engine, consumer (no serializer)
the draft 'timeout' key is consumer-side only and has no in-repo emitter, so the fallback is migration tolerance, not a live dual contract
engine uses the strict comparison work_ms > timeout_ms with status literals 'done'/'timeout' - frozen, must stay untouched
unittest-style tests executed with pytest from the repo root; new tests are additive only

inputs: frozen contract C1 (job wire schema) from stage-contract.json
frozen contract C2 (consumer timeout resolution order, owned by this task) from stage-contract.json

frozen_contracts.spec_ref: stage-contract.json shared_contracts[C1] - job wire schema; producer/engine frozen as-is
stage-contract.json shared_contracts[C2] - resolution order timeout_ms -> 'timeout' -> DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS; validate_job unchanged

non_goals: no change to pipeline/producer.py (key rename, signature, or default) - the wire-contract reference side is frozen (C1)
no change to pipeline/engine.py (comparison, status literals, default)
no removal of the deprecated 'timeout' fallback - removal is explicitly out of scope for this stage
no change to validate_job behavior and no new validation rules (e.g. no type-checking of timeout_ms)
no edits to existing test methods in tests/test_consumer.py, tests/test_producer.py, or tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py - additions only
no new files, modules, or dependencies
implementation_constraints: resolve by key presence, never by value: 'timeout_ms' present -> use its value (even 0); else 'timeout' present -> use its value; else return DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS
keep DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS defined in pipeline/consumer.py with value 30000

add the new test methods test_job_timeout_timeout_ms_primary and test_job_timeout_timeout_ms_wins_over_legacy to the existing TestConsumer class in tests/test_consumer.py (or a new class in the same file); do not create a new test file
run the suite from the repo root: python -m pytest tests/
at task close, pipeline/producer.py and pipeline/engine.py must be byte-identical to the baseline

deliverables.what: job_timeout in pipeline/consumer.py resolving timeout_ms -> 'timeout' -> DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (presence-based); validate_job and DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS unchanged in behavior
new unit test methods test_job_timeout_timeout_ms_primary (job {'timeout_ms': 500} -> 500) and test_job_timeout_timeout_ms_wins_over_legacy (job {'timeout_ms': 500, 'timeout': 123} -> 500)

acceptance_tests.description: consumer returns the producer-set timeout at the seam: producer.make_job('j1', {'cmd': 'x'}, timeout_ms=500) yields consumer.job_timeout(job) == 500 (the baseline returned 30000)
timeout_ms wins over the legacy 'timeout' key: job_timeout({'timeout_ms': 500, 'timeout': 123}) returns 500 and the 'timeout' value is ignored

fallback and default paths stay intact: a job with no timeout_ms but timeout=123 resolves to 123 (deprecated draft key still honored), and a job with neither timeout key returns DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000)
acceptance_tests.evidence: pytest tests/test_consumer.py -> all TestConsumer tests passed, including the unmodified test_job_timeout_reads_consumer_key (123) and test_job_timeout_default (30000)

acceptance_tests.description: engine semantics remain frozen under the fix: run_job(job with timeout_ms=100, work_ms=50) returns status 'done' and run_job(job with timeout_ms=100, work_ms=150) returns status 'timeout'
acceptance_tests.evidence: pytest tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py::TestPipelineE2E::test_pipeline_e2e_engine_timeout -> passed; diff shows pipeline/engine.py and pipeline/producer.py unmodified

acceptance_tests.description: all pre-existing unit tests remain green with zero test-case edits: producer and consumer suites pass unmodified, with the 2 new consumer test methods added
acceptance_tests.evidence: pytest tests/test_producer.py tests/test_consumer.py -> exit code 0, 7 passed, 0 failed (2 producer + 5 consumer, of which 2 are new)

failure_cases.scenario: job dict has neither timeout_ms nor 'timeout'
failure_cases.expected_behavior: job_timeout returns DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000); no exception is raised, matching the baseline behavior for an empty job

failure_cases.scenario: job dict has both timeout_ms and 'timeout' with different values
failure_cases.expected_behavior: job_timeout returns the timeout_ms value; the 'timeout' value is ignored per the frozen C2 priority order

failure_cases.scenario: job_timeout receives a timeout_ms value of 0
failure_cases.expected_behavior: job_timeout returns 0 (key-presence resolution, not value truthiness) - a 0 ms timeout is a valid, if aggressive, producer choice

failure_cases.scenario: a job is missing the 'id' or 'payload' key
failure_cases.expected_behavior: validate_job raises ValueError as before; the fix does not change validation, so the existing test_validate_job case passes unmodified

handoff.notes: T02 must start from the fixed consumer. If T02's new e2e cases fail against the fixed consumer, that is a T01 defect (report it in the T02 checkpoint) or a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST against C2 - T02 must not patch pipeline/ code itself.
